what: The fixed decoy prompts S2 ranks the true prompt against. Committed so the set cannot be chosen after the scores are seen, and NOT overridable from the command line: a caller who could pass their own decoys could pass trivially far ones and clear S2 by construction.

true_prompt_source.why: The true prompt is the one the #1864 reference render was actually taken at. Reading it from the manifest rather than from a flag means the prompt and the reference cannot disagree.

null_is: 1/(N+1) with N decoys, which is the chance that an argmax over N+1 prompts lands on the true one when the scorer is uninformative. It is derived, not chosen, and the tool prints it beside every S2 verdict.

decoys.text: A red fox walks slowly through a green summer forest at midday, cinematic.
A grey wolf walks slowly through a snowy pine forest at sunrise, cinematic.
A red fox sleeps curled up in a snowy pine forest at night, cinematic.
A busy city street at night with neon signs and heavy traffic, cinematic.
A close-up of a bowl of hot soup on a wooden kitchen table, cinematic.
An empty beach with turquoise water under a bright midday sun, cinematic.

why_these: The spec requires both a NEAR decoy and a FAR one. A set of only far decoys measures almost nothing: a scorer that can tell a snowy forest from a bowl of soup has been shown very little. The three near decoys each change ONE attribute the prompt names -- season, species, action -- so a render that got the season wrong is separable from one that got the animal wrong. The three far decoys are the floor: failing one of those is a broken instrument rather than a bad render.
